title: Multi-tenant SLO partitioning and noise-aware paging
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood's current SLO alerting runs cluster-wide burn-rate and threshold checks that are noisy for multi-tenant workloads. Small customers with noisy traffic and frequent deploys get disproportionate paging, while large customers' incidents can get lost in aggregated signals.

Goal:
Build a pipeline and runtime for per-tenant SLO partitioning and a noise-aware paging policy that: 1) attributes burn-rate and error spikes to tenants, 2) suppresses low-impact noisy pages, and 3) escalates high-blast-radius incidents faster. The feature should integrate with tracing hooks so individual sampled traces can be tied to tenant attribution and with the metrics/log pipeline for fast rollup.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- Per-tenant SLOs computed for latency (p95/p99) and error rate with 1-minute rollups and 5m burn-rate windows.
- Pages for tenants with <X monthly requests are routed to low-noise channel (Slack digest) instead of oncall by default, configurable by plan.
- Paging policy supports real-time escalation when a tenant's anomaly correlates with top-level service degradation or traffic shift.
- Paging volume reduced by >=40% in early experiment for non-enterprise tenants without increasing time-to-detect for high-impact incidents.
- Dashboard drilldown from cluster SLO => tenant SLO => example traces and logs.

Proposed approach:
1) Trace enrichment: add a lightweight tracing hook to API gateway and runtime to ensure each sampled trace has tenant_id, plan_tier, deploy_tag, and request_route. Hook will backfill from auth token headers and set a tenant_risk_score computed by Presto/feature-service.

2) Metrics/log pipeline changes: extend the metrics aggregator to maintain per-tenant time series keys. Use existing remote-write path but add cardinality controls (hot tenants vs cold tenants). Cold tenants get aggregated into a rollup group to avoid cardinality explosion; hot tenants are retained at full resolution. Use adaptive retention: hot tenants move to long retention while cold tenants are compacted.

3) SLO evaluation engine: implement tenant-aware burn-rate evaluation that factors in plan-weighted budgets (e.g., enterprise customers have stricter budgets and lower suppression). Burn-rate thresholds are computed relative to tenant baseline and cluster-level context.

4) Noise-aware paging policy: paging decision service consumes tenant SLO signals plus anomaly evidence from our anomaly detector. Policies:
   - suppress_page_if: tenant_monthly_qps < 10k AND estimated_customer_impact == low AND no correlated cluster degradation.
   - immediate_page_if: tenant_error_burst causes >5% cluster request loss OR tenant is enterprise_plan.
   - escalate_if: pages occur for same tenant across multiple regions or services within 10 minutes.

5) Dashboards and playbooks: new observability dashboard with per-tenant heatmap, burn-rate timeline, and quick links to sample traces. Add playbooks for low-noise incident flow and escalation steps.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Cardinality: detailed per-tenant SLOs increase metric cardinality. Mitigation: tiered retention, dynamic hot-tenant detection, and pre-aggregation.
- Latency vs accuracy: 1-minute rollups are a balance between timely paging and compute cost. We may need a sub-minute fast-path for particular enterprise customers.
- Privacy: tenant attribution will carry sensitive metadata; ensure PII-free tags and rely on tenant-id masking in logs.

Open questions:
- Exact thresholds for "cold" vs "hot" tenants and configurable defaults per plan.
- How to expose configurable paging preferences to customers (Console toggles vs support-only).
- Whether to route suppressed pages to SRE digest or to a customer-success queue.

Next steps (short-term):
- Spike: instrument gateway to attach tenant_id to sampled traces and run a 2-week data collection (ENG spike ticket).
- Implementation: wire enriched traces into existing trace-correlation pipeline and prototype per-tenant metric rollups on dev cluster.
- Experiment: run A/B test on 10% of non-enterprise traffic and measure page volume and time-to-detect metrics.

Links to artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Multi-tenant+SLO+Partitioning (draft)
- Experiment dashboard (dev): https://analytics.redwood.ai/dashboards/obs/tenant-slo-spike
